A marginal reminder adds: speed up source selection. Four statements are then offered, and only one of them follows from what the note actually says.

questions.stem: The note above supplies the evidence for a judgment about list of displays. One proposed reading is "To avoid using any displays". Which of the four options is actually supported by the passage?

options.text: To find the right source faster.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: the passage gives the controlling distinction: consulting the list speeds up finding the right source. On that basis "To find the right source faster" is the supported choice. Option A ("To impress supervisors") fails because it focuses on appearance; Option B ("To make the log longer") fails because it focuses on length; Option C ("To avoid using any displays") fails because it rejects display use.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Add missing agency to a report

stimulus.body: Read this source excerpt carefully: Adding who identified or caused the issue restores agency. A marginal reminder adds: name the responsible party. It is followed by four candidate interpretations, of which exactly one is supported by the wording of the excerpt.

questions.stem: The question turns on what the note above shows about passive methods. Given the proposal "The report's font", which choice is consistent with the evidence in the passage?

options.text: Who identified or caused the track work issue.

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: close reading of the note yields this rule: adding who identified or caused the issue restores agency. On that basis "Who identified or caused the track work issue" is the supported choice. Option A ("The report's word count") fails because it focuses on length; Option C ("The report's font") fails because it focuses on formatting; Option D ("More passive wording") fails because it increases vagueness.

questions.learningObjective: Decide when to trust a chain

stimulus.body: A claim traces through verified sources to an original log. a chain with verified links can be trusted. A marginal reminder adds: verify every link. Four statements are offered, and only one follows from the note.

questions.stem: A reviewer is weighing competing claims about attribution chains, among them "No, unless the source is recent". Based only on the excerpt above, which answer is the one the evidence warrants?

options.text: Yes, because the chain is long.
options.misconception: selects "Yes, because the chain is long" where the rule in the passage requires a different condition

options.text: Yes, if every link is verified.
No, unless the source is recent.

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: what settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: a chain with verified links can be trusted. On that basis "Yes, if every link is verified" is the supported choice. Option A ("No, because chains are unreliable") fails because it rejects all chains; Option B ("Yes, because the chain is long") fails because it selects "Yes, because the chain is long" where attribution chains requires a different condition; Option D ("No, unless the source is recent") fails because it focuses only on recency.
